summary: This feature explores how organizations are securing edge computing infrastructure as data processing moves closer to its source. It presents success stories involving AI-driven analytics, unified threat management, industry collaboration, machine learning anomaly detection, standards, and training. It concludes that adaptability, collaboration, and education are the common threads in edge security.
one_line: A feature on how companies secure edge computing through AI analytics, unified threat management, collaboration, standards, and workforce training.
key_facts: Delton Strategies, in a report released September 15, 2023, expected data generated by IoT devices alone to reach 79.4 zettabytes by 2025.
Edge computing processes data closer to its source, which reduces latency, saves bandwidth, and gives quicker responses to time-sensitive data.
Quantum Security Solutions is a startup founded in early 2024 by Maya Stephenson and Raj Gupta.
Quantum Security Solutions used AI-driven behavioral analytics and network segmentation to improve a multinational corporation's resistance to cyberattacks on its edge nodes.
The Unified Threat Management (UTM) model integrates firewalls, intrusion detection systems, antivirus software and more into one system managed from a central point.
By September 2023, SentinelTech had introduced a UTM device designed explicitly for edge networks; its CEO is Lucas Hendricks.

In November 2023, a consortium led by Pinnacle Computing and NewEdge Networks detailed a collaborative security initiative with a secure-by-design principle, enhanced encryption standards, and shared threat intelligence.
The shared-intelligence model has been especially helpful to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) that lack extensive cybersecurity resources.
EdgeGuard Inc. launched ML-powered anomaly detection tools in January 2024 that protect thousands of edge devices worldwide; its founder and CTO is Emily Zhou.
The Secure Edge Foundation (SEF) was formed in June 2024, and its EdgeSec Protocol has been adopted internationally by numerous corporations and governments.
Omega CyberSecurity has partnered with several tech corporations to develop specialized edge-security training modules.
Sandra Kim, Director of Education at Omega, says educating IT professionals on edge security builds 'the first line of defense'.
